title: architecting your digital abundance
content:
from my podcast: botanical studies of internet magic
listen on spotify / listen on apple

I'd like to share 5 distilled principles that transformed how I inhabit my business -- as a living ecosystem that centers my creative energy, above all else. learning, evolving, and embodying these principles took me so many years.

I'll share the journey and the hard lessons I learned in the process, and map these principles onto a 12 week itinerary for my new course, ⁠Digital Abundance⁠ -- as an alchemical process for deep re-alignment and re-imagining of what your business can become, this next season.

🧧 ⁠⁠⁠Digital Abundance⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ begins March 16

⁠my business is a hammock I weave by hand⁠

in the last episode, I named the core paradigm shift that integrated art and business — that creative wealth is wealth, and creative energy can feed and support an abundant life. and even though I realized this conceptually, it took me years to integrate, inhabit, and live this knowing. today, I want to go a bit deeper and share the actual principles and frameworks I've built, which are also the philosophical foundations of my new business class, Digital Abundance.

I want to share five principles with you that have informed every business decision that I've made. and I wouldn't even call it "made" — because it wasn't an active cognitive decision. it was me feeling my way into what kind of business could hold me and my creative energy. these five principles took me years to discover and evolve. I want to walk you through how I learned this, how it applies in my actual business, and then walk you through the shape of my 12-week itinerary for Digital Abundance as a conceptual map for how I might lead someone to reimagine a business in three months.

Digital Abundance is the spinal cord of my work about how to be an artist on the internet in a way that feels empowering in all senses of that word. so for me, teaching Digital Abundance is not just a class — it's also a threshold. it's catapulting me into my next dimension. what is possible with Digital Abundance? what happens after I've deeply lived the integration of art and business? what happens when I wholeheartedly trust my creative instincts to be in the driver's seat of my life? which is not to say that it's easy — it's scary a lot of the time. but it's also exciting. it makes me feel alive and like I'm fulfilling my destiny. that's not just what this philosophy is doing to me, but it's also what I want it to do for you, if you feel ready for this journey.

why philosophy matters

before we dive into the five principles — why does philosophy matter? it's not something abstract. it's reprogramming a core belief. when you change the programming, you're transforming a sense of who you are. you are changing your relationship to your own power. it happens at a deep embodied level. it gets integrated into your energetic architecture. and over time, you let this reprogramming ripple out into your day-to-day practice — how you make decisions in your life, how you move through the world and in your business. to me, that is what these philosophies do. not just a way of thinking, but a way of being and existing in the world.

the five core principles I'll talk about are: one, creative energy is the mother of money. two, your business must center you first. three, self-trust is your magical compass. four, your business is a living world. and five, sharing — or selling and marketing — is a practice of release.

principle one: creative energy is the mother of money

the first principle — and I feel like I've said this again and again on many different episodes — creative energy is the mother of money. and technically it's not just mother, but also matriarch, because the immaterial always creates the material.

as I mentioned in the last episode, your money will run out, but your energy multiplies. energy, when you put it into the right containers, is generative — it comes back to you. I learned this the hard way through many different contexts. through quitting my full-time job because it felt like violence to my soul to be putting my energy into someone else's garden. I stopped using social media because the energy I put into it just felt draining rather than generative. focusing on energy unlocked so much for me, especially when I started learning about human design and how I'm a projector.

and then perhaps the most profound, deepest learning experience was in 2024, when I experienced a betrayal while trying to open a coffee shop with my partner. I lost the money and experienced a wounding that was more than financial loss. it was feeling like my creative energy — which had created the money in the first place — was being completely diminished, minimized, and disrespected.

because money is a byproduct of business. it's not really the goal of your business to make money, even though money is what makes it a business. that's the paradox. money is not at the center — energy is. what I define as a business is a living resource. when you center money, you exhaust yourself trying to chase it. when you center energy, money follows.

principle two: your business must center you first

your business is actually all about you. you are the luminary — you're the light, the sun or the moon of your business. your light is what fuels energy for it. therefore, it must be centered around you.

and this is counter to standard traditional business advice. most traditional frameworks encourage you to think about your target audience, what marketable skills you have, customer avatars, pain points, value propositions, what will sell. but what I'm saying is — don't try to predict what other people will like or buy. because when you're other-centered, you are overriding your own desires, inspirations, impulses, and creating for an imagined avatar that may or may not exist. this might work in the short term, but I don't think it works in the long term — because when you override your own instincts, you won't be able to access your most generative, potent energy.

I'll add a nuance here. it's not about the binary of creating for yourself versus creating for the other. I used to find myself stuck in this pendulum swing of over-giving and then retreating, ghosting everyone, becoming very self-absorbed. sometimes I feel like we are so afraid of becoming this navel-gazing, self-obsessed artist who will never make money because we're not relevant to the outside world — that as a result, when we're trying to build something, we second-guess every instinct. we ask people what they want. we ask for advice. we ask what will sell.

it took me a long time to release the binary of that. because I believe you can be grounded and centered in yourself, in who you are — and at the same time, you can listen to the signals you receive from around you. paying attention to the other is just an extension of paying attention to yourself.

after you inhabit your own light, live in your luminary — that expression and projection of your light will draw people to you. when someone in your world says, "oh, I have trouble with x or y," or "I'm thinking about z," notice what it brings up in you. does it make you feel inspired to create something? think of those signals as part of the wind, like momentum. and when your energy aligns with that momentum, it gives a sense of direction to where your energy wants to go.

I will also say — when you are centering yourself in your business, it's important to distinguish between a desire for stability and safety versus what your soul or your creative instincts actually want. I fell into this trap many years ago when I taught a bunch of creative courses. people liked them, and I thought, oh, I could just iterate on this. this works, why not do it again? but each time I taught the same course live again, it made me tired. it kept me in a perfectionism loop until eventually I burnt out and took a two-year break from teaching altogether. the problem wasn't that I was teaching classes. the problem was the energy. if I sensed deeply into my center, I would discover that teaching the same classes didn't feel alive for me — just because I thought it would be safe or create stability doesn't mean it actually worked.

it's so crucial to be with yourself at the center. to let what feels alive guide your creative instincts, rather than what you think other people want from you.

principle three: self-trust is your magic compass

there is no right path or right way. there's only the path for you. and this is the foundation of my seasonal community, Labyrinth Library — that we are all in our own labyrinths, navigating the spiraling path alone and together. there are no templates, no fail-proof plans, no guarantees.

whenever I teach something, I don't hand you a plan with a checklist to execute, or a promise that if you follow this recipe exactly, you will be safe and rich and successful. instead, what I do is guide you along a journey of process — and suggest that through the process, you will develop the skills, experience, and discernment to navigate your own path. what I do teach is navigation in the dark. how to cultivate a sense of deep trust in yourself, no matter the weather.

self-trust is like a magical compass. it will always lead you to what you desire. therefore, it will lead you to the most generative reserves of your energy. therefore, it will lead you to your abundance.

when people come into my world asking to work with me or learn from me, what I discover is that they're just asking me to help them trust themselves. this is harder than it sounds. I struggled so much to trust myself because our society, our conditioning, our education is set up to override our deeper creative instincts. there's so much deprogramming work that must happen before we can fully trust ourselves — because when you outsource your authority to other people, to best practices, to "should" energy, you disempower yourself.

if you don't trust yourself, no one can save you. sorry, I had to say that. I know how dramatic that sounded.

I learned this through meeting a lot of resistance. discovering that working for myself, I couldn't apply the same techniques and strategies I did when I was working at a job. I couldn't measure my productivity or output or ROI in the same way. when well-intentioned, smart friends or family gave me advice, I realized — I can't take advice from anyone who hasn't done this exact thing that I'm doing. where does their authority come from? they have projections and ideas about what is right for me, but it's not from firsthand experience. and at the same time, I would hesitate when trying to take advice from other successful people in my field, because what works for them may not work for me.

the longer you're in business, the more you realize there is no objectively correct way. there is no safe path. there's only constant experimentation, grappling with process, asking hard questions, and finding your own way.

last winter, I recorded episode 24, "Underworld Business Practices" — when I realized how deeply lunar and underworld and Scorpio the way I run my business is. no one told me that I could do it. this is something I figured out myself. more than anything, I encourage you to apply these principles to your own practice and see if it works, how it works, what new insights come up for you.

in order to trust yourself, what's crucial to cultivate is a sense of embodied safety. I talk about this in my class, Money Juice Cleanse — that embodied safety comes before abundance. without safety, what you're holding is a bowl with a leak in it. nothing you fill it with will be enough. cultivating the capacity for self-trust is to take care of the container — that bowl of yourself. then your magic compass will lead you to magical places.

principle four: your business is a living world

your business can be a living, breathing world that you tend to — an ecosystem of its own. I use the word ecosystem frequently. my website is an ecosystem. I talk about it as a world, or a labyrinth. my business is also an ecosystem that exists beyond the container of my website.

and so if we believe that there is no right way to have a business, that business is not a machine you can set and forget — then part of what we are embracing is the principle of change. that things are always changing. your energy is changing. your life circumstances and needs are changing. the world is changing. the seasons are changing. change is the only constant.

I talk about this in my course, Creative Systems — that a system is meant to evolve, to adapt to each season of your life. and a business is a creative system. it's a living creature, organism, world that moves with you and holds you. it's something you take care of like a garden with seasons. sometimes there's new growth. sometimes things incubate and hibernate. sometimes they decompose.

I try to be in conversation with my business every season by asking: what do I desire to create this season? what season is my business in right now? what am I pouring my energy into? what does my business need from me — what kind of tending, planting, seeding, pruning, growing? and what do I need from this world to feel held, nourished, inspired, or safe?

remember that you can create whatever shape of business you want. a year ago, I wrote a piece on my website called "My Business is a Hammock I Weave by Hand" — because I realized I wanted a business that was flexible, malleable, lightweight, and something that allows me to rest. something I can lay down on. and of course, this hammock is made up of living things — vines and flowers and fruit — and it's always growing and changing.

your offerings are fluid shapes that hold your creative energy. not unlike making a shape for creative work — in fact, it's the same thing. it just happens to be something that people pay money for. I'll talk about pricing in Digital Abundance as an energy threshold. what it does is facilitate the exchange, deepen the exchange. the fact that something is paid versus your art being free to look at or read doesn't make one thing more valuable than the other. it's just a different quality of energy. the paradox is that art is a gift — it's priceless — and offerings can be created with gift energy while still having money as a container or threshold for them. I talk about this in a previous episode, "Make an Offering, Weave a Web."

and so when I have an idea for an offering, I have a creative spark, and then I'll ask myself — what does this want to be? does it want to be a course, a podcast episode, a workbook, a zine? what kind of energy does this offering want? what is the shape? and how can I allow this shape to feel flexible, to change with me over time? how can I tend to it over its life stages?

because I find that nothing feels like a failure, nothing feels stagnant, when you are inhabiting and moving with it. and then when you hold all of your offerings together as an ecosystem, as a living world — you'll see that your business contains many living, growing things, each in different seasons. some of them blossoming and flourishing, some of them incubating. each offering has its own rhythm and pace, its own channels and intensity of flow.

principle five: sharing is a practice of release

the last principle — sharing, or marketing and selling, is a practice of release. in episode 32, "Business Words I Never Use," I talk about how I don't use the word marketing or sales. I replace both of those words with sharing my work — part one and part two. because I think for most people, there's this split: you make the creative thing and it's joyful and fun, but then when you go and try to sell it or market it, you have to do this weird, sheepish, dreaded dance of — look at me, buy my thing. I don't experience it that way. and it took me a long time to deconstruct, deprogram, and release those feelings around marketing and selling.

the way I did this was by thinking about sharing my work not as pushing out, or promoting, or putting my stuff in front of people's faces — but as an act of surrender. an act of release. I talk about this in my class, Sharing Space Camp — that to share something is independent from how people receive it or don't receive it. it is simply the muscle of moving something from your internal private world into the external public world.

an example I like for this — think about how an egg starts as an embryo, hatches into a bird, and then flies away. when you share something, when you make an offering to the world, the moment you put it in a public place — your website, your newsletter — you're letting go. you're letting it fly away. because you don't have control over how many people sign up, or who visits, or who doesn't. you are completing a creative cycle. you're exhaling.

and I think many of us get stuck in this dance of trying to control the outcome. why isn't it working? I need to optimize this. how do I make it convert more? and I'm not saying don't evolve your offering or the ways in which you communicate it — but the anxious dance after you've shared something doesn't help that particular cycle. it's just anxiety from not being able to control what happens.

sharing an offering is a practice of surrender. you commit to being as true to yourself as you can when you write about the offering, when you talk about it, when you create its shape and container. and then when you announce it, when you let it go, when you open registration — there's very little you can do. more is not always better.

when you think about it that way, it strips away the weird energy or resistance we have around marketing and sales. because all it is is completing the creative cycle. if we think about creative work as the breath — the inhale is absorption, holding your breath is metabolizing, and sharing the work is the exhale. it's the end of one cycle of breath and the beginning of another. when you embody this, the practice of marketing and selling will just feel like breathing.

I don't even think about it as selling anymore. I have an offering that I value deeply because it comes from an essential, urgent, pulsing part of me. and there is a gated threshold — and the gate is there to ensure that this offering is aligned for whoever walks through it. because whenever we give our potent energy into an offering, it's vulnerable. we're putting ourselves into this thing. and it's important that that's recognized by the other.

the 12-week architecture of Digital Abundance

now that I've shared the five core principles at the foundation of how I've created my business over all these years — let me tell you about the 12-week architecture of Digital Abundance and my thinking behind it. this is not just a course syllabus, but how I would lead someone to reimagine a business in three months as an alchemical process for transformation.

each teaching module, each week, is built around four movements. the first is the philosophical framework — which is a practice of reprogramming. that's what we just went through: how you exist and move in your business. the second is practice and experimentation — I'm giving you the framework and the ideas, and I want you to play with the process. ask yourself questions and work on the muscle of self-trust through integrating and embodying the principles and experimenting with them in your own business. the third is working with resistance as your greatest teacher — as shadow work, as places for deprogramming. and the fourth is reflection and integration — taking what you've learned through each practice and process and letting it guide you forwards in your navigation, one step at a time.

I've divided the 12-week journey into four phases.

phase one: reprogramming
before anything else — meeting your resistance, clearing away the old stories around productivity, worthiness, creativity, and money. what if you thought of your creative energy as a form of abundance? is it accessible to you? how do you nurture it? how would that belief change your relationship to your business? then — what would happen if you put yourself at the center of your business? your longings, desires, impulses, inspiration. how would that be like a kind of business chiropractory? how would it reorganize, realign everything? what if you were to design your business around your energy? how would it change how you move through your business as a body?

phase two: business as a living world.
what is your business actually for? why does it exist? what is your business a vessel for? we'll do clarity and visioning work around the purpose, soul, heart of your business and set some intentions around it. I find that connecting to that heart core really helps me stay grounded and motivated when I'm feeling uncertain or existential about what I'm doing. this visioning work is essential. then we'll talk about your business as a living organism — ecosystem world with its own seasons and cycles of birth and death. in week five, we'll look at your different offerings — whether currently existing or newly imagined — each as separate containers for your energy. we'll sense and feel into each of them. notice what feels alive and what purpose each serves in the biodiversity of your current ecosystem. we'll look at your business as a connected web with nodes and channels that move between them — where is there circulation? where is there energy? where is there resistance and stagnation? how can we be more deliberate about tending to these different nodes and channels given where you're currently at in your life?

phase three: shaping the offering container.
we will center in on one offering and bring it from a series of incubating sparks to opening the offering container — which will be a slow and organic journey. the shape of your offering will emerge from the creative energy. we'll do visioning work: out of all the possibilities, which one feels the most alive? which one has the most generative energy? we'll sense into the raw material of this energy and what shape it wants to become. in week seven, we'll be working with this shape, letting it emerge through practice, process, and experimentation — and thinking about pricing as a threshold or container. in week eight, we'll use the form of what I call the invitations page — which is basically a sales page — as a way of continuing to create the boundaries around this offering. we'll also do work on imagining the ecosystem around the offering. if an offering is a node, then there are orbital rings around it, breadcrumb trails connected to other parts of your ecosystem. we'll talk about those interconnected pathways and how to see your offering as within a mycelial network of your entire creative world.

phase four: release and integration.
this is where you will practice releasing something into the world, watching what happens, and moving through resistance in real time. in four weeks, you will complete the invitations page, share it in your different channels, open registration for it, and walk yourself through the process of release and noticing what happens.

I tend to think about creating the shape of an offering — leading up to the point of signups and receiving payment — as actually a separate process from creating the offering itself. and so this itinerary takes you through the end of that first phase, because that is the hard part. the hard part is not creating the offering. it's making the shape, inviting people into that shape. it's like you've built this magical chariot — and now that people have come aboard, momentum will carry you the rest of the way.

and so by the end of our 12 weeks together, you will have a completely different relationship to your entire business ecosystem, to your creative abundance. you will have the chariot created, you will have fellow travelers on your chariot, and you'll be ready to depart on your journey. we'll spend the last week on integration — reflecting on the results of your experiment and setting a small intention for what's next, mapping this next season. because everything that you learn through this process is a trail marker for the next part of your journey.

building a business is not a sprint. it's not even a marathon. it's an expedition.

I don't know about you, but I intend to work for myself for the rest of my life. I realize that the only way this can be sustainable is if my chariot, my ecosystem, my world is always shape-shifting. and each time I sit down, it's my creative energy that is pulling me towards my next destination.

what I intend for you is not a perfectly evolved, finished business — but something so much more valuable. a true relationship with your creative authority. a deepened sense of self-trust. integration between your creative energy and the abundance that can and will overflow from it.

I'm also excited because I will be using this 12-week container to iterate my current business and incubate many different art worlds and micro-business projects that I haven't even talked about publicly yet. I'm not just teaching Digital Abundance — I am living it and experimenting with it alongside you.

closing

if you'd like to join me and our intimate cohort in this next live session, we will be beginning on March 16th. there will be weekly discussion sessions, a small group of fellow travelers, ongoing exercises and homework assignments, and one-on-one conversations and feedback with me.

thank you so much for listening to this episode. the best way to keep in touch is through my newsletter. as always, you can explore more of my work on my web world, my different courses, as well as working together one-on-one in my advising containers.

take care, until next time.
